question:
A 37-year-old woman comes for a follow-up prenatal visit at 18 weeks' gestation. At 12 weeks' gestation, ultrasonography showed increased nuchal translucency and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) was decreased by 2 standard deviations. Chorionic villus sampling showed a 47, XX karyotype. During this visit, ultrasonography shows a hypoplastic nasal bone, shortened femur length, shortened middle phalanges of the fifth digits with clinodactyly. A quadruple marker test would most likely show which of the following sets of findings?
 $$$ α-Fetoprotein (AFP) %%% Estriol %%% β-Human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) %%% Inhibin A $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increased nuchal translucency" -> "Possible Down syndrome" -> "Hypoplastic nasal bone" -> "Shortened femur length" -> "Shortened middle phalanges with clinodactyly" -> "Quadruple marker test" -> "↓ AFP" -> "↓ Estriol" -> "↑ β-HCG" -> "↑ Inhibin A" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Increased nuchal translucency" -> "Possible chromosomal abnormality" -> "47, XX karyotype" -> "Hypoplastic nasal bone" -> "Shortened femur length" -> "Shortened middle phalanges with clinodactyly" -> "Quadruple marker test" -> "↓ AFP" -> "↓ Estriol" -> "↑ β-HCG" -> "↑ Inhibin A" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Increased nuchal translucency" -> "Decreased PAPP-A" -> "Possible Down syndrome" -> "Hypoplastic nasal bone" -> "Shortened femur length" -> "Shortened middle phalanges with clinodactyly" -> "Quadruple marker test" -> "↓ AFP" -> "↓ Estriol" -> "↑ β-HCG" -> "↑ Inhibin A" -> 92%
analysis: The clinical findings and test results are suggestive of Down syndrome (Trisomy 21). The increased nuchal translucency, decreased PAPP-A, hypoplastic nasal bone, shortened femur length, and clinodactyly are characteristic features. In Down syndrome, the quadruple marker test typically shows decreased AFP and estriol, and increased β-HCG and inhibin A.
